scope: RP02 and 028 antibodies were crosslinked with hCD38‐ECD using CID‐cleavable crosslinker DSSO

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment is a chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (CXMS) study designed to map the binding epitopes of two different scFv antibodies (RP02 and 028) on the human CD38 extracellular domain (hCD38-ECD). The primary biological variable is the specific interaction/complex state between the antigen and the different antibody variants.

workflow: RP02 and 028 antibodies were crosslinked with hCD38-ECD using CID-cleavable crosslinker DSSO
LC MSn data of digested peptides were collected on Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid
The XlinkX detect program (Thermo Scientific) was used to search MS2 data and identify the list of putative DSSO-interlinked products
differential: The lysines crosslinked with scFVs were highlighted on the structure of hCD38-ECD (PDB 1yh3) for the epitope analyses.
search_parameters: Protein N-terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation (15.995 Da), carbamidomethyl cysteine (57.021 Da), hydrolyzed lysine DSSO (176.014 Da), and lysine DSSO Tris (279.078 Da) were selected as variable modifications.
three defined modifications on uncleaved lysines were chosen, including alkene (C3H2O, 54 Da), sulfenic acid (C3H4O2S, 104 Da), and thiol (C3H2SO, 86 Da) modifications.
Chymotrypsin was set as the enzyme with two missed cleavages being allowed

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The experiment is a structural proteomics study using chemical cross-linking (CXMS) to map epitopes. The primary goal is site identification (cross-links) rather than relative quantification of protein abundance.
